messages:
From: Amaya Torres <amaya.torres@finteq.io>

Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Deployment rights & audit deliverables — MSA questions

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Finteq is excited about Redwood for our on-prem gateway use case. A couple of legal items came up internally while we review the MSA/Order Form:

- License scope: our security team needs the MSA to explicitly allow on-prem deployment of the licensed model artifacts (we're evaluating a private VPC deployment in our GCP tenancy).
- Audit access: we need a mechanism for an independent security assessor to validate the deployment and logs. Our standard asks include either (a) limited read-only access to the environment for the auditor, or (b) a supervised snapshot with signed attestations.
- Escrow-like request: our procurement suggested a source-escrow or key-handback arrangement in case Redwood were to discontinue service. We understand this is sensitive — can you advise on alternatives?

Attaching the redline Finteq pulled from the MSA (they asked us to send this to your legal). Also copying our counsel (James Li).

Appreciate a quick run-through of what you can accommodate — we are on a tight procurement timeline (end of month).

Thanks,
Amaya Torres
Head of Cloud Platforms
Finteq

Hi Amaya — thanks for sending this over and for outlining the asks clearly. 

Quick responses while I loop in legal and our solutions engineer:
- License scope: we support private VPC and on-prem deployments. We can add explicit language that the Order Form grants the customer a hosted + private deployment license for the specified model version(s) and binaries used for serving.
- Audit access: we typically provide (1) an auditor workspace with read-only access to audit logs and metrics, and (2) timeboxed observer sessions for the auditor. Full shell/SSH access or handing over images isn't our standard.
- Escrow-like request: Source-code escrow is not something we offer. We have two common alternatives: a) a documented handoff playbook + signed export of configuration and container images under strict controls, or b) a KMS/HSM attestation and an agreed “key-handback” procedure with escrow agent on a narrow set of keys (not product source).

I'll forward to legal for formal redlines and to Marissa for procurement coordination. We'll aim to get a redline response and proposed alternate language by EOD.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: FWD: Deployment rights & audit deliverables — Finteq (legal notes)

Neha / team — see notes below (high level + proposed redline language). I attached a quick internal summary (internal_legal_notes.txt).

High-level positions:
- License scope: We can accept a clause in the Order Form confirming the customer's right to deploy the licensed model artifacts in their VPC/on-prem environment for the Term, limited to the specific model versions listed in the Order Form. Proposed line: "Seller grants Customer a limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable license to deploy the Licensed Artifacts in Customer-managed infrastructure for internal business purposes, subject to the restrictions in Section X (Use Restrictions)."

- Auditor access / audit scope: Do not provide interactive SSH or direct access to production hosts. Offer instead: (a) an independent auditor workspace with role-based, timeboxed read-only access to logs/metrics and (b) a supervised replay/snapshot where necessary. Proposed language: "Upon reasonable notice and at Customer's expense, Customer may engage an independent, mutually agreeable auditor to assess Seller's compliance with security obligations. Seller will provide auditor with time-limited, read-only access to relevant logs, metrics, and a supervised environment sufficient to perform the agreed scope."

- Escrow / key-handback: We cannot place product source code in escrow. For key-handback requests, legal is open to a narrowly scoped escrow of specific customer KMS keys or an attestations-based remedy. Conditions: (i) keys in escrow may only be used to decrypt customer data and must be released only upon specified trigger events (insolvency, sustained service outage beyond SLA, court order), (ii) escrow agent must be mutually agreed, (iii) use limited to restoring access to customer data, and (iv) Redwood retains ownership of product IP. Proposed clause: "If Seller ceases to provide the Services for a period exceeding 60 consecutive days, Seller shall deposit with an independent escrow agent a sealed copy of (i) the Customer-specific configuration exports and (ii) a key-handback token that enables decryption of Customer's encrypted data in Customer's environment. Use of any escrowed materials shall be strictly limited to restoration of Customer operations and shall not transfer any intellectual property rights to Customer."

Operational impacts / follow-ups for engineering: the KMS/key-handback option requires us to document the export and attestation procedure and confirm we can safely produce a configuration/container export that a customer can run in their environment. Marissa — can you coordinate with Solutions to validate feasibility?

If no product changes are needed, I can draft redline language for the MSA and Order Form; otherwise call with Solutions to scope engineering work.

-Laura
General Counsel (acting)
Redwood Inference

Hi Amaya / James — thanks for the clear summary and for sharing the redlines. Per our internal review, we believe there is a pragmatic path forward that keeps your security team comfortable while protecting Redwood's IP: 

1) Order Form insert for deployment rights: we will add the explicit license line (as Laura suggested) listing the permitted model versions.
2) Auditor access: we'll propose the auditor workspace + supervised snapshot approach; Redwood will accept reasonable auditor scope and will require a mutual NDA between the auditor and Redwood.
3) Escrow alternative: we cannot agree to source-code escrow. We are willing to include a KMS/key-handback clause with stringent triggers and an escrow agent; we will provide a documented export playbook and a test restore exercise during onboarding.

Next steps: Laura will send a redline of the MSA/Order Form this afternoon. Marissa will coordinate a short call with your Solutions/Cloud team to validate the restore/export process and timeline. If that sounds good, can we schedule the call for next Tue (3/23) or Wed (3/24)?
